processing: Made as a premium green tea, and today at least partly on automated lines. The exact steps are not published in accessible accounts.
harvest_season: Not documented in detail; as with other premium greens of the region, spring is the usual picking.
appearance_dry: Not well documented; typically slim, tender green leaf for a premium green of this class.
appearance_liquor: Not well documented; typically clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Not well documented; typically tender green shoots.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record is available. Expect what is typical of mountain greens: fresh, lightly sweet and vegetal.

brewing.notes: A general method for premium green tea, not one specific to this tea.

vintage_note: Not documented in detail. As usual for premium green tea it should be bought from the current year's harvest and drunk within about a year. The same local company also makes black, yellow and flower teas, so check which you are buying.
description:
Jiming Gongcha comes from Jiming township in Chengkou, the northernmost county of Chongqing, on the southern side of the Daba Mountains. It is counted among Chongqing's better-known green teas and is also simply called Jiming tea.

The area is described as mild, rainy and misty with acidic soils, and it lies close to selenium-rich belts, a point local promoters like to stress. Details of how the leaf is processed are not widely published.

There is little on record about the taste, so brew it as a normal premium green: water off the boil, short steeps, and a look at the leaf before you judge it.

The word gongcha means tribute tea, but treat that as part of the name, not as evidence. Look for a clear harvest date, and note that the name may also be used on other tea types from the same producer.
history:
A tribute past is implied by the name, but no accessible record says when or to whom tribute was paid. What is on record is recent: Chengkou Jiming tea received China's green food label in April 2002, the second tea in Chongqing to do so after Banan Yinzhen.

County figures for 2005 give more than 30,000 mu of tea gardens and more than 600 tonnes of tea, with 60 tonnes of it premium green. A 2024 newspaper report describes a demonstration garden of over 3,000 mu and a local company with automated lines.
